title: Runtime, Context Builder and Agent Backend

implemented the immutable built-in AssetCatalog with content fingerprints, fixed diagnosis-skill and LOGPARSE_TOOL bindings, typed ApplicationPortError channels, availability reports, and drift diagnostics
implemented strict CLAUDE_COMMAND tokenization and environment sanitization plus the cancellable AgentBackend with wall-time, log, Workspace, output, and complete process-tree controls

implemented secure read-only Workspace materialization for fixed Attachments and Artifacts, including r3 public archive-suffix and relative-path helpers, exact manifests, byte freezing, retry semantics, and no-dirfd fallback checks
implemented atomic output validation, secret scanning, deterministic failure normalization, proposal staging, and durable outcome publication through frozen ResourceStore and StateRepository Ports

implemented DiagnosisRuntime orchestration with fixed State reads, exact STATE_CORRUPT and STATE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED propagation, safe CASE_NOT_FOUND mapping, job-scoped broker lifecycle, post-close parse request auditing, and claim/request hash invariants

added injectable clocks, IDs, failure points, public Port Fake conformance coverage, deterministic component fixtures, and unit coverage for success, timeout, cancellation, corruption, drift, retry, size, hash, and cross-platform process behavior

tests.summary: 26 passed, 1 skipped in 1.69s; the skip is the Windows-only Job Object assertion on macOS
Runtime production and unit-test sources compiled successfully
1 passed in 0.31s; 6 manifests and all 13 owned files were checked for exact paths, sizes, and SHA-256 values

known_limitations: The Windows Job Object runtime assertion is platform-specific and was skipped on macOS; POSIX process-group and descendant termination tests passed on the current platform, and S08 must execute the Windows assertion on native Windows before claiming Windows release coverage.
risks: A caller-supplied synchronous AppendOnlyByteSink.write implementation that blocks forever cannot be safely interrupted by Python; shutdown waits for an already-started sink write so that no background writer can outlive backend return.

S08 must inject the same fixed AssetCatalog and job-scoped LogparseBrokerFactory pair owned by the composition root; using independently resolved LOGPARSE_TOOL products would correctly fail fixed-binding diagnostics.
integration_notes: The implementation head is 24dd5451d111a79244f7128ef4e502e7ddf5a61e and does not contain handoff/S04.json; the immediately following commit is reserved for this handoff only.

The former S04 ResourceStore and StateRepository typed-error request and broker parse-request audit request were resolved centrally by v1-contract-r2/r3; there are no outstanding contract change requests.

Workspace attachment filenames are derived only from immutable Attachment.name and content_type through derive_attachment_filename_suffix and workspace_attachment_relative_path, and consumers must use the exact manifest relative_path.

Runtime.execute propagates the identical StateRepository.read_case ApplicationPortError only for STATE_CORRUPT and STATE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, creates no JobOutcome for those faults, and retains the safe CASE_NOT_FOUND and ordinary-exception mappings.
AssetCatalog resolve, route_bindings, diagnose_bindings, and review_bindings use their frozen method-specific ApplicationPortError codes; check remains the negative AssetAvailabilityReport channel.

A broker session is closed before parse_request_bytes is audited; claim=None requires request bytes to be null, while claimed success, timeout, and failure all validate the frozen request hash invariant without matching exception text.

Catalog fixed-skill and LOGPARSE_TOOL fingerprints are execution inputs, not latest-state lookups; S07 remains authoritative for the real logparse product and S08 must preserve those ResolvedAsset refs byte-for-byte.

TREE resources are globally sorted before hashing and materialization, all reads remain anchored to the frozen inode, and per-file plus aggregate byte limits prevent replacement and size-growth races on dirfd and fallback paths.
